payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the book been moved behind the same flower shown in the source image?
node.criteria: complete: the book is behind the source flower in the edited image. partial: there is visible movement of the book toward being behind that flower, but the requested ordering is not achieved. absent: no movement toward that ordering is visible, even if the book or flower changed or was repositioned in an unrelated way. unknown: the source flower cannot be reliably identified in the edited image, or the depth ordering/progress cannot be judged.
node.binding: Target: the book. Reference: the single rose in the source image; track that same rose across images, not newly appearing flowers. Requested relation: the book is behind the rose in depth.

node_traces.evidence: The source rose is a red-and-yellow rose, but the edited image shows two yellow flowers and no clearly identifiable matching rose, so its depth ordering relative to the book cannot be judged.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding is already specific about tracking the source rose, but the traces repeatedly treat failure to identify it as automatically unresolved. Improve the decision procedure to compare source and edited images for identity using multiple cues (shape, red/yellow coloration, stem/position and surrounding context), while allowing for substantial appearance changes; do not equate a different-looking flower with proof of absence. Then assess the requested depth relation and visible progress independently: distinguish the book’s movement/repositioning from whether it is actually behind the matched rose, and use `partial` only when evidence shows movement toward that ordering. Here the edited image visibly contains two yellow flowers and a repositioned book, but the traces do not establish that either flower is the source rose or that the book moved toward being behind it. The repeated high-confidence `unknown` outputs alongside one `absent` indicate a criterion/routing ambiguity, not a transport or dependency failure (all checks are valid, queried, and dependency-free). Clarify when identity uncertainty warrants `unknown` versus when the requested relation/progress can still be judged; do not force the reference label or infer absence solely from color mismatch."}
